title: Notification Delivery
description: FEAT-009 / ADR-008 observability dashboard for the notification delivery pipeline. Panels 1-8 are Prometheus (via the otel-lgtm image's provisioned 'prometheus' datasource); panel 9 is the Loki/Tempo trace-and-log correlation ADR-008 §2/§3.1 wires up. Metric series names and datasource UIDs were confirmed against the running grafana/otel-lgtm stack (TASK-009-07), not transliterated from meter names.

list.name: delivery_id
list.label: delivery_id
list.description: Loki/log-only drill-down dimension (ADR-008 §4.3). Never a metric label. Leave blank to match all.

list.name: event_id
list.label: event_id
list.description: Loki/log-only drill-down dimension (ADR-008 §4.3). Never a metric label. Leave blank to match all.

list.name: client_id
list.label: client_id
list.description: Loki/log-only drill-down dimension (ADR-008 §4.3). Never a metric label - unbounded cardinality, denied outright by the MeterFilter. Leave blank to match all.

list.name: subscription_id
list.label: subscription_id
list.description: Loki/log-only drill-down dimension (ADR-008 §4.3). Never a metric label. Leave blank to match all.

panels.title: Delivery attempt latency percentiles (p50 / p90 / p99)
panels.description: ADR-008 §4.2: percentiles computed at query time from the notification.delivery.attempt.latency histogram buckets, never a client-side-precomputed quantile series. Buckets: 100ms,250ms,500ms,1s,2s,5s,7s,10s. A p99 above 5s (the worker read-timeout) is the signal, not a rendering artefact.

panels.title: Delivery attempt latency by outcome / status_class
panels.description: ADR-008 §4.1: the only two tags this timer carries. Average latency (rate(sum)/rate(count)) grouped by outcome and status_class - no other dimension is ever added.

panels.title: Relay dispatch latency percentiles
panels.description: ADR-008 §4.2: notification.relay.dispatch.latency, untagged, buckets 50ms,100ms,250ms,500ms,1s,2s,5s. Threshold line at challenge.relay.poll-interval (5s) - a cycle above it is the signal, a rendering choice, not an alert (ADR-008 §6 defers alerts).

panels.title: DLQ arrival rate
panels.description: notification.delivery.dlq.arrival is a counter (renamed from delivery.dlq.arrival by TASK-009-03) and resets on process restart - this renders rate(), never the raw monotonic total.

panels.title: DLQ depth
panels.description: notification.delivery.dlq.depth is a gauge polled from SQS GetQueueAttributes (ADR-008 §4.1.1). It goes STALE (holds its last value) on a failed poll and is NaN if it has never succeeded once - a flat line here is NOT automatically "the DLQ is fine"; check the app's poll-failure logs/traces before reading a flat line as healthy.

panels.title: Ingest request rate and latency (p99)
panels.description: http.server.requests, uri=/internal/events. ADR-008 §4.1: no bespoke ingest timer exists; this Boot-default timer is the ingest latency meter.

panels.title: Self-service request rate and latency (p99)
panels.description: http.server.requests restricted to the three delivered self-service paths (templated uri tag, not the expanded one): /notification_events, /notification_events/{notification_event_id}, /notification_events/{notification_event_id}/replay.

panels.title: Ingest and self-service error rate (4xx vs 5xx)
panels.description: http.server.requests split by status/outcome. A client's 4xx and the service's 5xx are different operational events and are never merged into one series.

panels.title: Delivery pipeline logs (click a trace_id to pivot into Tempo)
panels.description: OTLP log records in Loki. Each line carries trace_id/span_id attached by the appender from the live OTel context (ADR-008 §3.2, never hand-set); the Loki datasource's provisioned derived field turns trace_id into a link to Tempo, so a log line opens the same waterfall that spans ingest, relay dispatch and the delivery attempt across the SQS hop (§2). Optional filters below use the MDC keys §3.2 puts on every line (delivery_id, event_id, client_id, subscription_id) - the per-client drill-down path §4.3 states is a Loki/Tempo operation, never a metric label. content and response_excerpt are excluded from every query on this dashboard: §3.3 keeps them out of the log store entirely.

panels.title: Main queue depth (deliveries)
panels.description: notification.delivery.queue.depth (visible) and notification.delivery.queue.in_flight (received, not yet deleted) are gauges polled from SQS GetQueueAttributes on the deliveries queue, same pattern as the DLQ depth gauge (not originally in ADR-008 scope, added for live queue visibility). STALE on a failed poll, NaN if never succeeded - a flat line is not automatically "queue is empty", check poll-failure logs first.

panels.title: Circuit breaker transitions by direction
panels.description: notification.circuit.transition, tagged by direction (ADR-002 §3, ADR-006 §1.2). CLOSED_TO_OPEN = a worker tripped its local breaker (10 consecutive breaker-counting failures in production, 3 in the local profile). OPEN_TO_HALF_OPEN = the relay promoted a cooled-down subscription and admitted one probe. HALF_OPEN_TO_CLOSED = the probe succeeded, circuit recovered. HALF_OPEN_TO_OPEN = the probe failed again, cooldown escalates. A rising HALF_OPEN_TO_OPEN rate relative to HALF_OPEN_TO_CLOSED means a client has been down a long time, not flapping.

panels.title: Webhook stub — requests received (local profile only)
panels.description: http_server_requests filtered to /local/webhook-stub/receive - confirms the client (the local fake receiver, adapter/in/web/local/webhookstub) is actually being called, not just that the worker claims to be calling it. Split by status: a burst of non-2xx here is you exercising a forced failure (Force Status 500/429/400 in the Webhook Stub Insomnia folder) - expected during a retry-policy demo, not an incident. Absent entirely while the pipeline shows attempts = the worker never reached the client at all (egress block, DNS, wrong target_url).
